description: Masala Chai is a beloved Indian spiced milk tea, renowned for its comforting warmth and aromatic blend of spices. This traditional beverage offers a perfect balance of strong black tea, creamy milk, and a fragrant mix of ginger, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Enjoy a truly authentic experience that soothes the soul and invigorates the senses.

ingredients.notes: strong Indian black tea like Assam or Darjeeling

instructions.title: Prepare the Spices
instructions.text: Gather all your whole spices: green cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon stick, and black peppercorns if using. Lightly crush the cardamom pods and peppercorns using a mortar and pestle or the back of a spoon. Peel and grate or finely crush the fresh ginger.

instructions.title: Boil Water and Spices
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine 2 cups of water with the crushed spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, peppercorns) and the grated ginger. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Let it simmer gently for 2-3 minutes to allow the flavors to infuse.

instructions.title: Add Tea Leaves
instructions.text: Once the water is fragrant with spices, add the black tea leaves to the saucepan. Continue to boil for another 1-2 minutes, stirring occasionally. This step ensures the tea brews strongly and mixes well with the spice infusion.

instructions.title: Introduce Milk and Sugar
instructions.text: Pour in the 2 cups of whole milk and add the sugar to your taste. Stir everything together. Bring the mixture back to a rolling boil. Be careful not to let it boil over.

instructions.title: Simmer and Steep
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to low and let the chai simmer for at least 5-7 minutes. For a stronger flavor, you can simmer it longer, up to 10 minutes. Keep stirring occasionally to prevent the milk from scorching at the bottom of the pan. The longer it simmers, the more robust the flavors will become.

instructions.title: Strain and Serve
instructions.text: Once the chai has simmered to your desired strength, remove the saucepan from the heat. Carefully strain the chai through a fine-mesh sieve directly into serving cups, ensuring all the tea leaves and whole spices are removed. Serve hot and enjoy your authentic homemade Masala Chai.

tips: Always lightly crush whole spices just before use to release their maximum aroma and flavor into the chai.
For a stronger ginger kick, use a larger piece of ginger or finely grate it to increase its surface area.
Adjust the amount of sugar and milk to your preference; some like it sweeter and creamier, others prefer it less so. You can also use jaggery for an authentic touch.
